queries: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail arxiv MAST failure taxonomy

sources_considered.why: Peer-reviewed-track study of failures in multi-agent LLM systems. Context showing the kind of failure he describes is documented.

receipt.public_excerpt: This process identifies 14 unique modes, clustered into 3 categories: (i) system design issues, (ii) inter-agent misalignment, and (iii) task verification.

evidence_items.explanation: Shows that failures between agents in multi-agent LLM systems are real and common, which fits the scenario he describes. It does not test whether LLMs lack knowledge or thought, which is what his causal claim rests on.

unresolved_gaps: There is no agreed empirical test for whether LLMs have 'knowledge' or 'thoughts', so the causal premise cannot be checked.
The multi-agent consequence is phrased as 'might', which is not a firm claim.
